newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas extends gains on plant outages.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas extends gains on plant outages.

text.p: Canadian natgas prices continued to rise Wednesday due to plant outages and strength in the futures market, traders said.
"Field receipts are not showing up still," a Calgary-based trader said, adding he expected some downward pressure to surface Thursday as more supply becomes available.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.70/1.74 per gigajoule, up an average of eight cents from Tuesday and gaining 17 cents from week-ago levels.
July rose by a similar amount to C$1.66-1.69 per GJ.

At Sumas, Wash., prices jumped three cents on the day to $1.45-1.50 per million British thermal units (mmBtu). These prices were up about 11 cents from a week ago, lifted by a plant outage in British Columbia.
Prices will likely soften Thursday, traders said, as Westcoast Energy returns to service its 750 million cubic feet a day Fort Nelson gas plant in northeastern B.C.

The plant is expected to be back on line at midnight tonight, a company spokesman said, noting about 60 percent of capacity would be available on Thursday. Full restoration of the plant is anticipated in about two days, he said.
In eastern Canada, prices at Niagara climbed two cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s per mmBtu, indicating a weekly gain of five cents.
Supporting Niagara pricing over the last few days has been the rising futures contract, traders said. NYMEX's July Henry Hub gas futures rose to a high of $2.19 today, up 3.1 cents from Tuesday.
Temperatures in Toronto were still forecast to reach highs in the mid-70s over the next two days, according to Weather Services Corp.
